correctness.rationale: For fixed q, complete coloured stars are counted by q times the number of weak q-compositions of m-1; this includes the q singleton types. The components form a multiset, giving the stated Euler product and the exact fixed-type deletion bijection. In the tilted geometric model, the expectation and variance follow by Riemann sums: the leading coefficient of a_m is q/(q-1)!, and the mean kernel integrates to Gamma(q+1) zeta(q+1), giving q^2 zeta(q+1). The next-order O(t) relative mean estimate holds by integrability of the leading kernel derivative and the lower-order coefficient terms; q=1 has no lower-order terms. For the Fourier check, on the band m in [1/(2t),1/t] the geometric parameters are bounded away from zero and one, each logarithmic modulus costs at least a constant times 1-cos(m theta), and a_m is of order t^(-(q-1)). For |theta|<=t this yields Gaussian decay; for t<=|theta|<=Mt the band Riemann sum has a uniformly positive mean, and above Mt the geometric-sum bound O(1/|theta|) is smaller than a fixed fraction of the band length for large fixed M. The Lyapunov bound follows from the geometric third centered absolute moment bounded by a constant times e^(-mt)/(1-e^(-mt))^3 before multiplying by m^3; summing gives O(t^(-(q+3))), which is o(sigma_t^3). Normalized central inversion and the tail bounds then give the asserted local limit at integral mean. The additional factor |1-exp(i h theta)|<=h|theta| in the difference gives O(sigma_t^-2) absolute error, hence o(t) relative error. Undoing the exponential tilt gives the stated leading fixed-shift ratio with the negative sign. The EF strategy pairs fresh components by truncated profile and has enough unused copies and leaves for r moves. A union bound over the finite canonical set gives the fixed-sentence rate, and the colour-1 singleton deletion with shift one proves sharpness. The finite checker was inspected, not run; it tests only finite coefficients, deletion, and coarse scaling, not the asymptotics or EF argument.

evidence: Theorem 1.4 gives a leading exponential, a finite set of strictly lower powers in its exponent, and an expansion in inverse powers with relative error O(n^(-min((2L-alpha)/(2(alpha+1)),R/(alpha+1)))); (1.11) gives the leading exponential coefficient explicitly. The RT_1 and earlier logical criteria cover qualitative saturation but are not the source of the leading constant.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Here f(m) is a positive polynomial in m on all positive integers. Thus (P1) holds for arbitrary L. Writing f(m)=sum_j c_j m^j gives L_f(s)=sum_j c_j zeta(s-j), so (P2) holds for arbitrarily large nonintegral R: simple positive poles, at most a double pole at zero after multiplying by Gamma(s)zeta(s+1), and only simple possible nonzero nonpositive poles; the line at -R is regular. Polynomial growth on vertical strips gives (P3). The largest pole is alpha=q with residue q/(q-1)!, also for q=1. The theorem covers all fixed q and can make the power remainder exponent strictly larger than 1/(q+1).

evidence: For alpha=q the coefficient A_1 from (1.11) is (1+1/q)(q^2 zeta(q+1))^(1/(q+1)). The lower powers in the exponential are strictly less than q/(q+1), and the remaining terms are a constant times a power of n times an inverse-power series with arbitrarily fine remainder.
Deleting r copies of one fixed star type gives a fixed shift h=r ell. Failure of a finite rich-family threshold is bounded by a sum of one minus these shifted ratios.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: In the log of u_(n-h)/u_n each lower exponential power has shift o(n^(-1/(q+1))), the power prefactor contributes O(1/n), and each finite inverse-power term changes by O(n^(-1-beta)) with beta>0. Choose the relative remainder o(n^(-1/(q+1))) at both arguments. The top term shifts by -h[q/(q+1)] A_1 n^(-1/(q+1))=-h kappa_q n^(-1/(q+1)). Exponentiation gives the exact frozen ratio; h=1 gives the sharpness witness and constant. Standard EF saturation requires only finitely many truncated profiles with r copies; one fixed complete type per profile suffices. The finite union bound therefore gives the claimed upper rate without another quantitative asymptotic. Neither the distinct logical wording nor a direct reproof of the partition ratio supplies an independent new fact.

value.rationale: Sharp convergence in this natural measure is a well-motivated question. But the asserted speed and exact obstruction are obtained by inserting a positive polynomial weight into an existing stronger theorem, taking a fixed-shift ratio and applying the standard finite-profile saturation argument. The record does not identify an independent structural obstacle, a new bound beyond that implication, or a distinct regime. A direct specialization proof is useful exposition but does not rescue the stated contribution under the scientific value standard.
